_about: Optional written view per upcoming game, keyed by ESPN game id: {"text": "...", "sources": [urls], "written_at": ISO}. Shown on the game page as 'Analyst view' (locker-room news, trade rumours, a player facing his former team...). Never mixed into the numbers.

401910019.text: Both teams are on the second night of a back-to-back. Golden State, who have lost four straight and were beaten by 22 in Dallas, will rest Draymond Green (right elbow), and Stephen Curry (oblique) is not re-evaluated until Nov 25. Memphis are buoyant after a franchise-record eighth straight road win in Cleveland, even with Ty Jerome sidelined, and beat the Warriors in October after a late collapse. The angle leans towards Memphis.

401910020.text: Damian Lillard makes his first trip back to Milwaukee since tearing his Achilles there, saying 'I'm not going to limp out of here', after warning Giannis that 'the grass isn't always greener'. The Bucks are 1-14 with 11 straight losses, the worst 15-game start in franchise history, and come in the night after Giannis beat them in Miami. Deni Avdija (foot) is questionable for Portland. The emotional edge and the mood both lean clearly towards Portland.

401910021.text: Karl-Anthony Towns returns to Minnesota as a champion, calling it 'bittersweet' because he wanted to win one there, and he has averaged 36 points in two earlier visits; his extension talks with New York have stalled. Minnesota are 8-3 without Anthony Edwards, with Ayo Dosunmu stepping up. Towns' motivation is the main off-stat factor, so the angle leans slightly towards New York.

401910022.text: San Antonio's 12-game winning streak ended against Detroit and Dylan Harper is out with left hip soreness after slipping on the court. The Clippers were stunned by 25 in Utah, Tyronn Lue admitted 'we couldn't stop them', and Brandon Ingram is still listed out, although Yanic Konan Niederhauser is cleared to debut. A Spurs side wanting a response against a reeling opponent: the angle leans clearly towards San Antonio.

401909305.text: Charlotte blew an 18-point lead and lost in overtime at the Lakers after Charles Lee kept Brandon Miller and Coby White out of overtime because of minutes limits, a call fans criticised; Grayson Allen has concussion-like symptoms. Atlanta are flying after handing Oklahoma City its first home loss, but are thin at point guard with CJ McCollum out at least four weeks and face Detroit next. The angle leans towards Atlanta, with a small letdown risk.

401909306.text: Brooklyn's 30-point loss to Chicago left Julius Randle calling it 'embarrassing' and questioning the team's pride and effort, and Jordi Fernandez agreed. The Nets are reportedly listening to calls on almost anyone, including Michael Porter Jr. on his expiring deal. Orlando just had a four-game winning streak ended in Philadelphia but remain 5-3 on the road. The angle leans towards Orlando, unless the public criticism sparks a Nets response.

401909307.text: Indiana lost in Houston with Rick Carlisle ejected for the first time this season, Andrew Nembhard missing a second game with a sore hip and Tyrese Haliburton still out; the front office is shopping for wing upgrades, which can unsettle the names in the rumours. Cleveland are without Evan Mobley for at least another week and lost at home to Memphis. The angle leans mildly towards Cleveland.

401909308.text: Toronto have lost six straight, Darko Rajakovic blamed 'mental mistakes, lack of communication', Kawhi Leonard will miss at least four more games and RJ Barrett picked up a new hamstring injury. Detroit finish a 3-1 road trip at home and won without Cade Cunningham, whose knee soreness is described as mostly precautionary. The angle leans clearly towards Detroit.

401909309.text: Washington snapped an eight-game losing streak in Toronto behind Anthony Davis and a career night from AJ Dybantsa, which eases some pressure on Brian Keefe, whose job The Athletic says could be in danger; Trae Young has publicly backed him. Chicago have won three of four, Josh Giddey says 'I like where the team's going', and they lost the October meeting. The angle leans towards Chicago.

401909310.text: Dejounte Murray's trade request has found no significant market, per ESPN, and he is away from the team with an ankle injury; New Orleans are 5-11 and on the first night of a back-to-back. Oklahoma City have lost four of five, including a first home loss, and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander called it a new challenge; Alex Caruso (hip) is questionable. Both sides are unsettled; the angle leans towards an Oklahoma City response at home.

401909311.text: Utah have turned the mood around with back-to-back wins over the Clippers and the Lakers, Keyonte George scoring 30 in both, though this is their third game in four nights. Phoenix have won six of eight and are 2-0 on a five-game road trip, and they deny talking to New Orleans about Dejounte Murray even as Jalen Green's name circulates. Two confident sides; the angle is close to neutral with a slight lean to Phoenix.

401909312.text: Alperen Sengun's status is uncertain after he was poked in both eyes in Indiana (scratched left cornea), in a heated game with five technicals; this ends a four-game Rockets road trip. Denver, booed at home last week, responded by coming back from 17 down to beat Boston with Jamal Murray's go-ahead shot. The angle leans slightly towards Denver, more so if Sengun sits.

401909313.text: Sacramento are 1-13 after a franchise-first 0-7 homestand, Doug Christie is in the last fully secured year of his deal and says 'the seat is hot, always', and Domantas Sabonis had a visible exchange with Zach LaVine on Wednesday. The Lakers had a nine-game winning streak ended in Utah and Austin Reaves (heel) is day-to-day after an encouraging workout. A Lakers side wanting a response against a fractured opponent: the angle leans clearly towards Los Angeles.
